messages:
Maria H: heads-up — after yesterday's deploy that split prefill/decode into separate queues, we're seeing a 7-12% p99 tail increase on 8k-context jobs. Not universal but spikes line up with short-prefill long-decode mixes.
Kevin L: ugh. saw a small blip in the canary logs but assumed noise. any flame graphs?
Maria H: attaching inline sample from cpu flame: kernel-switch hotspots during handshake, lots of tiny kernel launches when decode batches are starved while prefill drains.
Sanjay R: pattern makes sense — prefill keeps forming microbatches and then decode side sees irregular kernel shapes, kernel selector keeps flipping to smaller matmul kernels, which hurts throughput.
Anya: can we confirm KV cache thrash? If prefill is evicting warm KV then decode will re-warm and cause extra kernels.
perf-bot: perf-check: canary-2026-02-12 -> p99_latency +9.8% for model/redwood-7b-qlora. KV_hit_rate decreased 1.9pp in same window.
Kevin L: thanks perf-bot. Maria, can you paste the batching config?
Maria H: config snippet: 
```
batcher: 
  prefill: {max_delay_ms: 6, token_budget: 256, max_batch_tokens: 4096} 
  decode:  {max_delay_ms: 8, token_budget: 512, max_batch_tokens: 8192} 
  handshake_policy: separate_queues
```
Kevin L: token_budget ratio looks odd for our traffic. decode token_budget should be lower for short-turn jobs; separate_queues needs tunable token cap per active stream.
Sanjay R: quick profiling note — sequence-length histogram shows bimodal: many requests with prefill ~64 tokens then decode ~1024 streaming. Prefill-heavy interleaving causes decoder queue starvation.
Anya: what about kernel affinity? If phase-aware scheduling marks kernels by avg seq len, selector could pin to larger kernels for decode and smaller for prefill. Right now selector observes blended statistics.
Maria H: current selector uses moving average per model_id only. No phase tags. We could tag metrics with phase (prefill|decode) and maintain separate kernel hit counters.
Kevin L: agree. Two options: (A) surface phase to kernel selector and keep separate kernel histograms, or (B) force decode to route to reserved kernel pool via kernel_hint. Option A seems lower risk.
Sanjay R: also saw KV cache churn on the GPU — warmup windows were too short. decode requests re-pull KV pages. We should extend kv_priming grace for decode streams to 2s instead of 300ms.
Anya: propose experiments: 
- A1: enable phase-tagged kernel stats (soft rollout)
- A2: increase decode kv_priming_grace_ms to 2000
- B1: reduce prefill token_budget to 128 for short requests
- B2: add handshake token_cap to limit prefill-draining during high backlog
We can run A1+A2 first.
Maria H: prioritized. I'll push phase tags to metrics pipeline and bump kv grace in canary tomorrow.
perf-bot: queued bench job: canary/phase-tagging-run-1 (ETA 2h). Baseline: p99=212ms, p50=18ms.
Kevin L: small note: kernel selector hotpath is latency sensitive. Keep memory footprint small when adding phase keys. Use a fixed-size LRU keyed by (model,phase) not unbounded map.
Sanjay R: yeah allocate a two-slot per-model phase state: prefill and decode. Avoid per-stream cardinality.
Anya: also add a soft fallback: if phase-tagged kernel not seen enough samples, fall back to model-level decision. Prevent oscillation during rollout.
Maria H: will add min_samples=200 in selector before switching.
Kevin L: can we also add a debug metric that counts kernel flips per second for a model-phase? would make regressions visible.
perf-bot: metric created: kernel_flip_rate_{model}_{phase}. Initial canary numbers in 3h.
Sanjay R: after A1+A2, if tail still bad, we should try B1+B2 (token budget adjust). Reducing prefill token_budget to 128 should collapse microbatches.
Anya: and one last thing — streaming backpressure: decode max_delay_ms 8ms is too aggressive for long decodes, allows small partial batches to go. Increase to 12ms as an alternative.
Maria H: noted. Plan: deploy phase-tagging + kv grace 2s + kernel_flip metric to canary. Observe 24h, then toggle token_budget and decode delay if needed.
Kevin L: thanks. @perf-bot, remind us in 24h to check regression dashboard.
perf-bot: reminder set for 24h.
Maria H: tl;dr — likely root is blended kernel stats + kv churn due to separate queues. Fix approach: keep phase-aware selector + longer kv grace, then tweak token budgets if needed.
Anya: +1. if you want I can help with the selector PR review.
Maria H: appreciate it — will tag you.
Kevin L: if this stabilizes can we add a small e2e test that simulates bimodal seq lengths to catch regressions?
Sanjay R: I'll sketch the test harness after the canary results.
Maria H: thanks everyone. closing for now, will post results in thread. :rocket:
